answers.answer: No. SCOPe (release 2.08, the current release per /api/v1/releases/current) puts all three groups in one fold, f.21 "Heme-binding four-helical bundle", but in three separate superfamilies, so it does not support treating them as one homologous superfamily. The three superfamilies are: f.21.1 "Transmembrane di-heme cytochromes" (the transmembrane di-heme cytochromes, with Formate dehydrogenase N gamma subunit f.21.1.1 as a family); f.21.2 "Fumarate reductase respiratory complex transmembrane subunits" (the fumarate reductase/succinate dehydrogenase transmembrane subunits SdhC/FrdC and SdhD/FrdD, family f.21.2.2); and f.21.3 "Respiratory nitrate reductase 1 gamma chain" (the respiratory nitrate reductase gamma chains). The shared fold reflects a common heme-binding four-helical-bundle architecture, which SCOP uses to group proteins with similar topology whether or not they share ancestry. Superfamily is the level that asserts probable common evolutionary origin, so the fold grouping does not imply homology between these superfamilies. Limits: (1) an architectural match is not evidence of homology, and the bundle and heme-binding could be convergent or ancient; (2) moving these members into one superfamily would need external evidence such as a structure-based superposition showing a conserved core, a profile or HMM-based sequence link with significant scores, or a curator decision in a SCOPe update, none of which this API supplies; (3) function and cofactor role should not transfer across superfamilies from the shared heme-bundle fold alone (for example, nitrate reductase gamma chain function should not be inferred from the di-heme cytochrome superfamily); (4) when choosing representatives for any comparison, use the superfamily-specific SCOPe nodes rather than the fold node, since the fold node spans more than one evolutionary lineage.

The three superfamilies are: f.21.1 "Transmembrane di-heme cytochromes" (the transmembrane di-heme cytochromes, with Formate dehydrogenase N gamma subunit f.21.1.1 as a family); f.21.2 "Fumarate reductase respiratory complex transmembrane subunits" (the fumarate reductase/succinate dehydrogenase transmembrane subunits SdhC/FrdC and SdhD/FrdD, family f.21.2.2); and f.21.3 "Respiratory nitrate reductase 1 gamma chain" (the respiratory nitrate reductase gamma chains). The shared fold reflects a common heme-binding four-helical-bundle architecture, which SCOP uses to group proteins with similar topology whether or not they share ancestry. Superfamily is the level that asserts probable common evolutionary origin, so the fold grouping does not imply homology between these superfamilies. Limits: (1) an architectural match is not evidence of homology, and the bundle and heme-binding could be convergent or ancient; (2) moving these members into one superfamily would need external evidence such as a structure-based superposition showing a conserved core, a profile or HMM-based sequence link with significant scores, or a curator decision in a SCOPe update, none of which this API supplies; (3) function and cofactor role should not transfer across superfamilies from the shared heme-bundle fold alone (for example, nitrate reductase gamma chain function should not be inferred from the di-heme cytochrome superfamily); (4) when choosing representatives for any comparison, use the superfamily-specific SCOPe nodes rather than the fold node, since the fold node spans more than one evolutionary lineage.
